text: Awarded the L. Meltzer Universitetsstiftelse Prosjektstipend (NOK 73,300) as principal investigator for *Engaging stakeholders to democratise integrated assessment modelling for climate mitigation*.
Published my first methodological contribution to the field’s flagship journal, *System Dynamics Review*, on feedback-story analysis as a method for integrating causal loop diagrams.
Began teaching *System Dynamics Modelling Process* (GEO-SD304) as instructor of record, after three years as its teaching assistant.

Graduated my first Master’s student as principal supervisor, Benedikt Tusch, whose thesis built a conceptual system dynamics model of pro-environmental behaviour change and contributes to my WorldTrans work.
Re-appointed to the System Dynamics Programme Board as the PhD representative, University of Bergen.

A semester project I supervised, by Anna R. Siemer, led to a co-authored paper presented as a Student Plenary at the student-organized colloquium of the International System Dynamics Conference in Chicago: *Modeling public transportation attractiveness in system dynamics: The significance of safety perception*.
Invited by European Young Engineers to run a Beer Game workshop at their 50th conference in The Hague, Netherlands: *Brewing success: Learning to manage supply chains with the Beer Game*.
Began my PhD at the University of Bergen as a Research Fellow in the EU Horizon Europe project [WorldTrans](https://worldtrans-horizon.eu), working on participatory integrated assessment modelling.
